complete.problem: Work out 25% of 60 by turning the percent into a fraction of the whole first, as in scene s3.

steps.text: Step 1: percent means per hundred: shade twenty-five cells out of one hundred on the hundred-grid - that shaded amount is 25%.
steps.annotation: A count out of one hundred: 25% is 25 out of 100, whatever the whole in the question is.

steps.text: Step 2: 25% of 60: divide into quarters: 25 out of 100 simplifies to one quarter, so split 60 into four equal parts and take one: 60 / 4 = 15.
steps.annotation: One of four equal parts of a whole: 25 out of 100 simplifies to one quarter, so 25% of a quantity is a quarter of it.

steps.text: Step 3: the takeaway: a percent is out of one hundred - turn it into a fraction of the whole first, and 25% of 60 comes out as one quarter of 60, which is 15.
steps.annotation: The full amount the percent is taken of: in 25% of 60 the whole is 60, so the answer is a share of 60.

complete.selfExplanation: Explain why the 25 in 25% counts out of one hundred, so 25% of 60 cannot be 25.

steps.text: Step 1: use the same per-hundred idea: 10% is 10 out of 100, which is one tenth.
steps.annotation: Percent means per hundred, so the 10 in 10% counts out of one hundred.
Split the whole 60 into ten equal parts and take one part.
Check by rebuilding: ten tenths of 6 make 60 again.

faded.selfExplanation: The first step is shown. Say how the whole splits into tenths, and what 10% of 60 comes to.

paired.problem: Write 25% as a fraction in its simplest form and explain the step.
paired.solution: 25% = 25/100 = 1/4: divide the top and the bottom by 25.
